name: Percentage of health facilities with a functional EMR system installed
numerator_source: EMR deployment register / system inventory (outside the EMR). Proxy only: central Prometheus, facilities with increase(artemis_routed_message_count{address=~"sync.facility.*"}[30d]) > 0
disaggregations_supported: facility (sync address sync.facility.<code>) for the proxy
disaggregations_missing: county; facility type (not in the EMR or the broker)
notes: Site: central (proxy only). Not SQL: the proxy is a PromQL query on central monitoring, the same series SyncStatusService and the SyncFacilitySilent rule read. 'Sent sync traffic in 30 days' means installed and in use, but says nothing about facilities never enrolled, so the denominator must come from the register. Prometheus retention bounds how far back the proxy reaches.

name: Percentage of targeted facilities with EMR fully rolled out to all planned clinical service points
numerator_source: EMR deployment register (planned modules/service points per facility, outside the EMR). Proxy: per facility, encounter types with >=1 encounter in the last 30 days (openmrs.encounter.encounter_type, date_created)
encounter_types: all clinical encounter types; exclude system ones: Check In; Check Out; Attachment Upload; Order; Lab Results; Bed Assignment; Cancel ADT; Transfer Request
disaggregations_supported: facility; service point (encounter type or form) for the proxy
disaggregations_missing: the planned service-point list per facility (not in the EMR)
notes: Site: both for the proxy (facility: its own; central: all facilities, grouped by the root of encounter.location). The proxy is direct SQL; no flat table. The planned list needs a register. The content-site-* packages record per-site configuration but not a rollout plan.

name: Percentage of EMR facilities with reliable power source (grid, solar, or generator) for EMR operation
notes: No power or UPS telemetry exists: distribution/monitoring scrapes only the sync sender at the facility, with no node or UPS exporter. Facility-to-central silence (SyncFacilitySilent) cannot tell a power outage from a network outage.

name: Percentage of EMR facilities with functional internet/network connectivity
numerator_source: Facility readiness assessment / network monitoring. Proxy: central Prometheus, facilities with increase(artemis_routed_message_count{address="sync.facility.<code>"}[24h]) > 0, or not firing SyncFacilitySilent
denominator_source: EMR facilities (deployment register or broker enrolment)
notes: Site: central (proxy). Not SQL: PromQL. The proxy measures 'reached central' and not 'internet up'. A facility with no clinical activity sends nothing and looks disconnected. Facility Prometheus has no connectivity probe (no blackbox exporter). Needs a probe if the monthly figure is to come from monitoring.

name: Percentage of offline-captured records successfully synced to central server within 48 hours
numerator_source: Central: openmrs_mgmt.<entity>_hash.date_created (dbsync stamps LocalDateTime.now() when central first applies the record) joined on <entity>_hash.identifier = openmrs.<entity>.uuid; lag = <entity>_hash.date_created - <entity>.date_created <= 48h; entities encounter, patient, visit (encounter_hash, patient_hash, visit_hash)
denominator_source: Facility: count of openmrs.<entity>.date_created in the period at that facility; this is the only true denominator. Central has only the records that arrived (a lower bound) until facility counts reach central (sync-eip.md 5.5 reconciliation, not built). Facility backlog: openmrs_mgmt.debezium_event_queue.date_created and sender_retry_queue.date_created older than 48h
disaggregations_supported: facility (central: root of encounter.location or openmrs_identity.patient_link.facility_location_uuid); entity type; month
disaggregations_missing: per-record send time: dbsync keeps none (sender queue rows and receiver_sync_msg/receiver_synced_msg rows are deleted once processed)
notes: Site: both, with different meanings. Central = share of facility records created in the period whose first application at central was within 48h. Facility = records still unsent after 48h (the backlog; the queues are transient so there is no history). Direct SQL across schemas (openmrs + openmrs_mgmt); no flat table. Gaps: (1) the facility EMR DB user has no SELECT on the facility openmrs_mgmt (central grants it, facility initdb does not); (2) records from the initial snapshot must be excluded (they need a per-facility sync go-live date); (3) clock skew: capture time uses the facility clock and receipt time the central clock (NTP is a go-live requirement, sync-eip.md 5.7); (4) the hash date_changed is overwritten on every update, so only inserts are measured reliably; (5) a true denominator needs reconciliation counts from each facility.

name: Percentage of patient encounters with complete core minimum dataset entered
numerator_source: openmrs.encounter (encounter_datetime, location_id, visit_id, form_id) + encounter_provider (non-voided) + obs (non-voided, per CMDS concept) + encounter_diagnosis (OPD) + person (gender, birthdate) + patient_identifier (MOH HRN), evaluated against a CMDS definition keyed by encounter type and form name
denominator_source: openmrs.encounter non-voided, in period, clinical encounter types with a CMDS definition
forms: anc-initial; anc-followup; family_planning; newborn-pnc; pnc-visit; first_and_second_stage_of_labor_and_delivery-mch; third_stage_of_labor_and_delivery-mch; tb_screening-national; aefi-national; immunization-national; opd_consultation_form; triage_form
encounter_types: ANC Initial Visit; ANC Follow-up Visit; Labor & Delivery; Postnatal Visit; Family Planning; TB Screening; Consultation (shared by OPD and five national forms, so key on form); Triage
disaggregations_supported: facility; encounter type; form; provider; month
notes: Site: both, with the same definition. The facility is authoritative. Central measures the same thing over synced rows (obs, encounter, encounter_provider and encounter_diagnosis are all watched tables), but lags by the sync backlog. Direct SQL per encounter; no flat table needed, though for OBS-heavy months a flat table would be cheaper (defer). Gap: no CMDS definition exists. The forms' required flags are inconsistent (L&D, Mother PNC and the national ANC/PNC/FP/immunization forms have none) and the form engine already enforces them, so they cannot serve as the definition alone. Proposal and location are in emr-ops-gaps.md.

name: Duplicate patient record rate (percentage of patients with more than one active record)
numerator_source: Facility: non-voided patients sharing normalised given+family name, birthdate and gender (person_name, person), or sharing a non-voided identifier value of the same type; plus person_merge_log for merges done. Central: openmrs_identity.patient_link grouped by the primary CPI (cpi.primary_cpi_id), counting groups with >1 patient_uuid from the SAME facility_location_uuid; openmrs_identity.match_review status='OPEN' reported beside it
denominator_source: Facility: non-voided patients (patient.voided=0). Central: distinct primary CPIs (cpi where primary_cpi_id IS NULL)
disaggregations_missing: probabilistic match band (scoring not built; only exact National ID auto-links)
notes: Site: both. Facility = within-facility probable duplicates by heuristic. Central = records of one person at the SAME facility as linked by the CPI service. Cross-facility records of one person are expected by design (ADR 0005 link-never-merge) and must NOT count as duplicates. Direct SQL; no flat table. Gaps: central detection covers only exact National ID matches (optional at registration) until Fellegi-Sunter scoring is built, so the rate is a floor; the review-queue owner is unnamed (ADR 0005).

name: Percentage of clinical encounters entered into EMR on the same day of service
denominator_source: openmrs.encounter voided=0 with encounter_datetime in period, clinical encounter types
encounter_types: all clinical encounter types; exclude system ones: Check In; Check Out; Attachment Upload; Order; Lab Results; Bed Assignment; Cancel ADT; Transfer Request
disaggregations_supported: facility; encounter type; form; creator (encounter.creator); month
notes: Site: both, with the same definition. dbsync preserves date_created: it writes via its own JPA entity (BaseCreatableEntity maps date_created from the payload), not through the OpenMRS AuditableInterceptor, so central gives the facility's value. Direct SQL; no flat table. Caveats: forms that default encounter_datetime to now make back-entry look same-day unless the user changes the date; retrospective entry after a paper-register outage is legitimate and should be reported beside it (lag in days as a distribution); both columns are local time on the facility clock.

name: Percentage of trained clinical staff actively using the EMR (logged in and entered >=1 record in the last 30 days)
numerator_source: Facility: users with user_property 'lastLoginTimestamp' (epoch ms, written by core HibernateContextDAO on each login, last value only) within 30 days AND >=1 row created in 30 days (encounter.creator/obs.creator/patient.creator/visit.creator with date_created). Central: record creation only (creator preserved by sync; user_property is not synced)
denominator_source: Staff trained on EMR: not in the EMR. Needs a 'trained' marker on the user (new capture). Interim proxy: non-retired users holding a clinical role (users, user_role)
notes: Site: facility (login + activity); central (activity only, since user_property is not a watched table). Direct SQL; no flat table. Gap: the training register is outside the EMR. Propose a user-level marker (e.g. a person attribute type 'EMR training date' on the user's person, which syncs) or take trained counts from the training register. Login history is not stored (see EMR-OPS-011), so 'logged in within 30 days' relies on the single lastLoginTimestamp property.

name: Ratio of patient encounters captured electronically to total patient encounters at EMR facilities
numerator_source: openmrs.encounter non-voided, in period, clinical encounter types (or visits: openmrs.visit)
denominator_source: Total encounters EMR + parallel paper: paper-register tallies are not in the EMR. Candidate: HMIS monthly attendance from DHIS2 or a monthly facility tally
encounter_types: all clinical encounter types; exclude system ones: Check In; Check Out; Attachment Upload; Order; Lab Results; Bed Assignment; Cancel ADT; Transfer Request
disaggregations_supported: facility; service point (encounter type); month (numerator only)
notes: Site: both for the numerator (direct SQL). The denominator needs a new monthly tally, or a pull of HMIS attendance from DHIS2 at central; no DHIS2 link exists (see EMR-OPS-014). No flat table.

name: Average number of EMR logins per active user per week
numerator_source: None persisted today. The authentication module 2.3.0 keeps active logins in memory only (UserLoginTracker) and logs events at INFO with marker AUTHENTICATION_EVENT; core keeps only the last login (user_property lastLoginTimestamp). Proposed: a log4j2 JDBC appender (module README pattern) into a new table, e.g. liberiaemr_login_event (user uuid, event type, timestamp)
denominator_source: Active users: distinct users with >=1 login event in the week (same new table), or the EMR-OPS-009 activity definition
disaggregations_missing: all, until login events are persisted
notes: Site: facility. Logins at central are central users only; facility login events should not be synced (keep the new table out of eip.watchedTables). Direct SQL once the table exists; no flat table. Gaps: add the table (liberiaemr liquibase) and the log4j2.xml appender to the backend image; spike whether the O3 REST session login emits UserLogin events when no authentication.scheme is configured (none is configured in this repo); set retention on the table (it is personal data).

name: Percentage of clinical and data staff at EMR facilities trained on EMR use
notes: If the EMR-OPS-009 'trained' user marker is added, the numerator could come from the EMR (users with the marker), but staff posted stays an HR figure.

name: Staff turnover rate among trained EMR users (indicator of retraining need)
numerator_source: HR records cross-referenced with training register
notes: Weak proxy: users.retired=1 with date_retired in period (account deactivated), if the ICT SOP deactivates accounts on departure. It cannot tell leaving post from other deactivations.

name: Percentage of EMR facilities successfully transmitting aggregate data to DHIS2/interoperability system
numerator_source: None today. No DHIS2 push exists: the dhis2-export service in the central compose names an image nothing builds (profile dhis2, off), and integration/dhis2/mappings is blocked on MOH data-element mappings. Once built, it needs a persisted transmission log (org unit, period, dataset, import summary status, timestamp)
denominator_source: EMR facilities (deployment register or enrolled facilities)
disaggregations_supported: facility/org unit; dataset; period (after the change)
disaggregations_missing: all, until the exporter and its log exist
notes: Site: central, since the only designed push runs at central on facilities' behalf. That conflicts with the decided model of local reporting at each facility (see emr-ops-gaps.md). 'On-time' needs a deadline per dataset from the MOH. Direct SQL on the exporter's log table once it exists; no flat table. Blocked on the MOH mappings.

name: Percentage of patients with a unique patient identifier matched consistently across visits/facilities
numerator_source: Facility: patients with >=2 visits who have exactly one non-voided MOH Health Record Number (patient_identifier by type) whose value did not change across the period (no voided HRN rows). Central: primary CPIs with >=2 visits across linked records where every linked record carries the same non-voided National ID, or the group was linked on basis NATIONAL_ID (openmrs_identity.patient_link.basis, national_id)
denominator_source: Facility: patients with >=2 non-voided visits (openmrs.visit). Central: primary CPIs whose linked records have >=2 visits in total
disaggregations_missing: cross-facility matches outside National ID (scoring not built)
notes: Site: both. Facility = consistency of the facility-scoped MOH HRN (uniqueness LOCATION; idgen prefix per site). Central = consistency of the person key across facilities via CPI; National ID is optional (Required=false), so the central rate largely measures National ID capture. Direct SQL; no flat table.

name: Percentage of EMR-eligible reports/dashboards actively used by county and national M&E teams for decision-making
numerator_source: Review meeting minutes. Partial usage proxy: reporting module table reporting_report_request (requested_by, request_datetime, status, report definition) at central
disaggregations_missing: county (users carry no county); use in a meeting
notes: Site: central (proxy). Running a report is not using it for decisions; the indicator needs minutes. Dashboards outside the reporting module (e.g. Superset, if adopted) would need their own usage log.

name: Patient record retrieval time (average time to access a patient's full history at point of care)
notes: System-side proxy only: the gateway nginx uses the default access log format, with no $request_time; a log format with request timing on patient-chart REST/FHIR calls, scraped to monitoring, would give server latency, but not the human retrieval time the indicator defines.
